recentItems.title: Hong Kong’s first robot-run convenience stores
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Beijing-based company Galbot has launched its first humanoid robot-operated convenience stores in Hong Kong. The venues include two outdoor shops in Hung Hom and Wan Chai and an indoor store at Kai Tak. SCMP reporter Llewellyn Cheung got a first-hand look at the store to see what the fully automated shopping experience was like.

recentItems.title: Funerals and DNA tests in Nepal a week after disaster
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Families continue to perform last rites for victims who were swept away by last week’s flash floods in Nepal. At least 1,200 people have been confirmed dead following the disaster while more than 4,000 others have been reported missing. Authorities have started collecting DNA samples from survivors to help identify flood victims.

recentItems.title: Air China aircraft grounded in New York after refuelling mishap
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

A Boeing 747-8 operated by Air China was grounded at New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport after a fuel truck drove away while refuelling. The incident early Monday reportedly damaged the aircraft’s fuel ports and caused a fuel spill on the tarmac. The Chinese flag carrier’s Beijing-bound flight was cancelled, leaving passengers stranded at the gate.

recentItems.title: Research shows China-Nepal floods impossible to outrun
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

The first Chinese study of the Nepal-Tibet disaster found that the surface velocity of the debris flow from the flash floods was moving at about 19 metres (62ft) per second when it first struck Gyrong Port in Tibet. The speed is almost twice the average pace of the world’s fastest man, Usain Bolt, when he set the 100-metre record in 2009. While it is still not clear what caused the avalanche that triggered the flooding, Chinese scientists say that rising global temperatures are causing ice in the Himalayas to melt faster. At least 16 people have died and more than 546 others remain missing on the China side of the disaster zone, while the death toll on the Nepal side has reached 1,058 with 4,606 still missing.

recentItems.title: Search and rescue efforts continue after China-Nepal disaster
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Read more about this topic: https://sc.mp/vhndz

More than 100 Nepalese citizens and one British national have been rescued during the most recent search operations following devastating flash floods, according to the Nepalese army on Tuesday. The confirmed death toll exceeded 1,000 on Tuesday, as rescuers used heavy machinery, helicopters and excavators to try and reach thousands of people still missing one week after the Himalayan disaster left a trail of destruction in the region.

recentItems.title: WATCH: Chinese President Xi Jinping at Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
recentItems.description:
President Xi Jinping is in Kyrgyzstan for the annual Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). The Chinese leader is scheduled to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Indian President Narendra Modi, as the three nations discuss plans to deepen strategic ties. Observers expect the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s 25th anniversary summit to offer clues to China’s ambitions for a more multipolar Asia.
